lessonRef.title: Craft or structure analysis: firsthand and secondhand accounts of the same event

studentTask.text: Today's focus: firsthand and secondhand accounts of the same event. Essential question: How do I build an opinion on evidence and read someone else's reasons fairly? By the end of this lesson you should be able to: Analyze how the text is built and what that construction accomplishes for firsthand and secondhand accounts of the same event. You'll need: course notebook or an accessible digital equivalent; pencil, keyboard, or another accessible response tool; the assigned passage in print, on screen, or read aloud.

guidedSupport.text:
Work through this with a facilitator, tutor, or on your own if you're ready:
- Welcome and retrieval: Open with a brief accessible retrieval prompt connected to today's lesson. Ask the learner to recall, predict, or pose a question before any instruction.
- Word study and fluency: Two minutes of word work on the vocabulary today's lesson requires, then one short passage read for accuracy and phrasing. Reading aloud is optional.
- Model or mini-lesson: Walk through a passage naming its structural or craft choices and what each one does for a reader.
- Guided practice: Analyze a second passage together and argue for the structure or craft label from evidence.

If you get stuck:
- If prerequisite gap: Return to the smallest prerequisite today's lesson depends on, model it once with a text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
- If decoding or fluency barrier: If the barrier is reading the words rather than today's lesson, drop to the word or phrase level, reread the line, then return. Do not reteach today's lesson while decoding is the actual obstacle.
- If repeated error pattern: Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short retrieval check in a later session.

independentEvidenceTask.text: The learner analyzes a third passage and justifies the label with two pieces of evidence. When finished: Name the structure or craft choice and the evidence that rules out the alternative.
